AGENDA

PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA 90274
Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.

  MINUTES OF THE OCTOBER 11, 2022
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

CALL TO ORDER - 6:35 P.M.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE - The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Lozzi.

ROLL CALL

PRESENT: Mayor Lozzi, Mayor Pro Tern Roos, Councilmembers Kemps, McGowan
and Murdock

ALSO PRESENT: City Manager Prestwich, Interim City Attorney Rusin, Chief of Police
Best, Public Works Director Seims, City Treasurer Greenberg, City Support Services
Director Hannah, and City Clerk Chaney.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kemps, Seconded by Councilmember Murdock to
approve the agenda.
AYES: Lozzi, Roos, Murdock, McGowan, Kemps
Noes: None

MAYOR'S REPORT - MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

Mayor Lozzi reported on the recent free compost event, the upcoming hazardous waste
pickup, the upcoming Lunada Bay Harvest Festival and the fall decorations.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

City Manager Prestwich provided updates related to City communications, the new
Management Analyst, and the upcoming retirement of the Chief of Police.

Chief Best introduced Community Relations Officer Merlin David who provided a report
on the Pink Patch Project fundraiser taking place during the month of October.

CEREMONIAL

Chief Best conducted the ceremonial swearing-in of Officer Garrett.

PRESENTATION

Valerie Gorsuch presented on behalf of Neighborhood Watch

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

The following individuals addressed the City Council: Al Martinez, Chad MacAllister, Susan Griego,
Desiree Myers, Cindy Jones, Joan Davidson, Janice Maier, Blake Gillman, and Jim Parker.

CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1-7)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
OICTOBER 11 , 2022
 ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Murdock, Seconded by Councilmember McGowan
to approve the consent agenda.
AYES: Lozzi, Roos, Murdock, McGowan, Kemps
Noes: None

1.  APPROVAL OF WARRANT REGISTERS

  Reviewed and Approved Warrant Register(s) of October 11, 2022.

2.  PARKLANDS COMMITTEE ACTIONS OF SEPTEMBER 8, 2022

  Received and Filed.

3.  CONSIDERATION OF ORDINANCE 22-756, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES AMENDING CHAPTER 8.18: MANDATORY
  COMMERCIAL AND MULTIFAMILY RECYCLING OF TITLE 8: HEALTH AND
  SAFETY OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE

  Presented on second reading, by title only; adopted a motion waiving further
  reading; and adopted proposed Ordinance No. 22-756: An Ordinance of the City
  of Palos Verdes Estates, Amending Chapter 8.18: Mandatory Commercial and
  Multifamily Recycling of Title 8: Health and Safety of the City of Palos Verdes
  Estates Municipal Code.

4.  CONSIDERATION OF ORDINANCE 22-757, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES AMENDING CHAPTER 13.08: STORM
  DRAINS AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT AND POLLUTION CONTROL
  OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE

  Presented on second reading, by title only; adopted a motion waiving further
  reading; and adopted proposed Ordinance No. 22-757: An Ordinance of the City
  of Palos Verdes Estates, Amending Chapter 13.08: Storm Drains and
  Stormwater Management and Pollution Control of the City of Palos Verdes
  Estates Municipal Code.

5.  ADOPTION OF A PROPOSED RESOLUTION WAIVING CERTAIN
  PROVISIONS OF THE CITY'S PURCHASING PROCEDURES THRU
  DECEMBER 31, 2022 FOR THE SOLE PURPOSE OF OBTAINING FUEL FOR
  THE CITY'S FUELING STATION STORAGE TANK

  Adopted Resolution R22-43 waiving certain provisions of the City's Purchasing
  Procedures for single purpose authority up to $50,000 for obtaining fuel for the
  City's fueling station storage tank through December 31, 2022.

6.  SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION OF THE LUNADA BAY HOMEOWNERS
  ASSOCIATION TO HOLD ITS HARVEST FESTIVAL AT LUNADA BAY PARK
  ON OCTOBER 16, 2022

  Reviewed and Approved.

7.  PLANNING COMMISSION ACTIONS OF SEPTEMBER 28, 2022

  Received and filed.

  Wei Shi addressed the City Council.
8.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES AND
  ROBERT LINKROUM FOR VIDEOGRAPHY

  Reviewed and Approved.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
OICTOBER 11, 2022
 ORDINANCES

9.  CONSIDERATION OF ORDINANCE 22-758, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES AMENDING CHAPTER 9.20: UNLAWFUL
  POSSESSION OF A CATALYTIC CONVERTER OF THE CITY OF PALOS
  VERDES ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE

Chief Best provided the staff report. City Council asked clarifying questions regarding
administrative citations and fines and referring violations to the District Attorney for
prosecution.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kemps, Seconded by Councilmember
  McGowan to introduce on first reading, by title only, proposed Ordinance No. 22-
  758: An Ordinance of the City of Palos Verdes Estates, Amending Chapter 9.20
  Unlawful Possession of a Catalytic Converter of the City of Palos Verdes Estates
  Municipal Code.
  AYES: Lozzi, Roos, Murdock, McGowan, Kemps
  Noes: None

NEW BUSINESS

10.  CONSIDERATION OF LICENSE AGREEMENT FOR ONE NONSTANDARD
  DRIVEWAY, ONE STANDARD DRIVEWAY, TWO STANDARD DRIVEWAY
  APPROACHES, NONSTANDARD STAIRS, AND STORMDRAIN LINES IN
  THE CITY RIGHT-OF-WAY FOR 1524 VIA FERNANDEZ

  Public Works Director Seims provided the staff report and answered clarifying
  questions.

  Ravi Sreerama addressed the City Council.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kemps, Seconded by Mayor Pro Tern Roos
  to approve the License Agreement for one nonstandard driveway, one standard
  driveway, two standard driveway approaches, nonstandard stairs, and
  stormdrain lines; and (2) Authorize the City Manager to execute such documents
  on behalf of the City.
  AYES: Roos, McGowan, Kemps
  Noes: Lozzi, Murdock

11.  CONSIDERATION OF OPTIONS RELATED TO AUGMENTATION OF TREE
  TRIMMING FUNDING

  Public Works Director Seims provided the staff report and answered clarifying
  questions with the Urban Forester Carl Moritz.

  Don Briggs addressed the City Council.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Murdock, Seconded by Councilmember
  Kemps to allocate an additional $156,000 for tree trimming and $44,000 for right
  of way clearance and fire abatement and that staff bring back an amendment to
  the Travers contract to perform the work.
  AYES: Lozzi, Roos, Murdock, McGowan, Kemps

12.  DELEGATIONS OF AUTHORITY & CONTROL OVER BANK ACCOUNTS

  City Treasurer Greenberg provided the report.
  Desiree Myers addressed the City Council.
  The City Council provided direction to staff and the City Treasurer to return to the
  City Council with clear recommendations and this item was continued to a future
  meeting.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
OICTOBER 11, 2022
   The City Council took a recess from 9:37 to 9:50 p.m.

13.  QUARTER 1 UPDATE ON PROGRESS OF FISCAL YEAR 2022-23 CITY
  COUNCIL WORK PLAN TASKS

  City Manager Prestwich provided the report.

  Councilmember McGowan asked that an item related to the Zoning Map update
  be added, and that staff return to Council with a scope, budget and timeline of
  the project as soon as possible.

  Councilmembers also requested that the potential technology update of the
  Council chambers be added to the IT section of the work plan.

MAYOR AND COUNCILMEMBER REPORTS

Councilmembers Murdock and Roos reported on their work with the Tennis Club on the
concession agreement, as well as their ad hoc work with La Venta, noting an upcoming
community meeting on October 20th.

Councilmember McGowan reported his attendance at the JPIA Risk Management Seminar and
his committee work on disaster preparedness on the peninsula.

Councilmember Kemps attended the Chamber's legislative update and reported on the
Metropolitan Water District's upcoming project on improved water supply reliability.

Councilmember Murdock requested an update on the oversized vehicle ordinance and
to make sure the Council is receiving Traffic Safety Committee minutes. She also
mentioned having a longer-term tentative agenda list.

Councilmember Kemps mentioned the Library District's 'Doors Open Peninsula 2023
celebrating 100 years of history on the peninsula' project with their Archivist Monique
Sugimoto and requested a future agenda item to discuss the City's involvement.

ADJOURNMENT TO TUESDAY, OCTOBER 25, AT 6:30 P.M.

The meeting was adjourned at 10:23 p.m.
